You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the tetragonal space group I-42d, number 122, with Hall symbol I -4 2bw. The input cell is rhombohedral-like in its metric: all three input lattice vectors have equal length 7.01049566 Å, with the angle between the first and second vectors equal to 128.94092151°, the angle between the first and third also 128.94092151°, and the angle between the second and third equal to 75.10565212°. This input cell contains eight atoms in total, with composition Al2Ag2Se4.

The relationship between the input fractional coordinates q_input and the standard fractional coordinates q_standard is given by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the matrix P has rows (0.5, −0.5, −0.5), (0.5000000000000001, −0.5, 0.5), and (−0.5, −0.5, 0.5), and the origin shift s is (−5.551115123125783×10⁻¹⁷, 0.5, 0.25). Thus, to recover the original input-cell description, one applies this affine transformation to the standard coordinates; conversely, the standard conventional description is obtained from the input cell through this same relation. The very small first component of the origin shift is effectively zero, differing from exact zero only at the level of floating-point representation.

In the standard frame, the independent atomic content consists of three orbits. Aluminum occupies Wyckoff position 4b with representative fractional coordinate (0, 0, 1/2) and multiplicity 4. Silver occupies Wyckoff position 4a with representative (0, 0, 0) and multiplicity 4. Selenium occupies Wyckoff position 8d with representative (x, 1/4, 1/8), multiplicity 8, and the single independent positional parameter x = 0.7138750000000003. These three orbits together generate the full atomic arrangement under the I-42d symmetry operations.

The aluminum and silver sublattices are therefore fixed special-position sublattices: Ag at the origin-type 4a site and Al at the 4b site displaced by one-half along the standard c direction. The selenium sublattice is more general within this symmetry, lying on the 8d orbit with y fixed at 1/4, z fixed at 1/8, and x equal to 0.7138750000000003. Because the input cell is nonstandard relative to the conventional setting, the declared input composition Al2Ag2Se4 should be understood in that original cell, while the standard-frame orbit multiplicities describe the conventional symmetric representation. No precision corrections to the listed atomic positions are required; the given coordinates are already the corrected values at the stated rounding precision of six digits.
